review_notes: Read the whole target file and the definitions and lemmas used by its two `simp only` calls: correctionData_linear/quadratic/metric, algebraic_formula, rawQuadratic, rawFrame, rawInverse, and clamp. Only one concrete simp-interface issue is well supported. The other simp calls are `simp only` or `simpa only` with explicit lemma lists, and they do not depend on an ambient simp set. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether adding the attribute would break any other proof. A grep for `correctionData_quadratic` in the library finds only this one use, which fits that conclusion.

findings.declaration: EulerAllOrderDriftCorrection.ExactLiftedPacket.source_equation (use of correctionData_quadratic, which is declared in PacketCorrectionSourceData.lean)
findings.problem: The three projection lemmas for `correctionData` are a parallel family. `correctionData_linear` and `correctionData_metric` are tagged `@[simp]`, but `correctionData_quadratic` is not. It has the same shape: a coefficient of `correctionData D P κ hκ Z G` rewritten to an explicit `FInv`/`F`/`fderiv` expression. Its right-hand side is built from `D.FInv.field` and `fderiv` of `D.F.field`, which are not `correctionData` terms, so rewriting cannot loop. Because the attribute is missing, a plain `simp` unfolds the linear and metric coefficients but leaves the quadratic one stuck. The only call site, this proof, works around that by naming all three lemmas in `simp only`.
findings.proposed_change: In PacketCorrectionSourceData.lean, add `@[simp]` to `correctionData_quadratic`, matching `correctionData_linear` and `correctionData_metric`. The `simp only` call here can then keep the explicit list for robustness, or become a plain `simp` with the remaining unfolding lemmas. Check that `correctionData_quadratic` does not conflict with `quadraticTower_apply`. Neither lemma is currently `@[simp]` in the sources I inspected, so I expect no conflict, but I haven't confirmed this by compiling.
findings.benefit: The simp interface for `correctionData` becomes uniform. Future uses will normalize the quadratic coefficient to the same explicit `FInv`/`fderiv F` form as the linear and metric coefficients, and callers will not have to remember a special-case lemma.
